meta.title: Guided Journal Finder — Open Journal Browser
meta.description: Match your manuscript to open-access journals, institutional deals, and funder requirements using local semantic search.

header.heading: Find the right open-access journal for your manuscript
header.intro: Answer four quick questions about your manuscript, funder, and budget. We match locally against {institution} deals, open-access models, and journal scope.

manuscript.heading: Tell us about your manuscript
manuscript.description: Paste a working title and abstract (or a short summary). We match topic similarity against journal scopes and recent articles.
manuscript.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Droplet formation dynamics in microfluidic T-junctions
manuscript.abstractPlaceholder: Paste your abstract, key methods, or a few sentences describing the study…
manuscript.charCountNeeded: Add at least {remaining} more characters across title and abstract

microfluidics.title: Interfacial dynamics and breakup regimes of viscoelastic droplets in microfluidic T-junctions
microfluidics.abstract: We investigate the formation and pinch-off dynamics of viscoelastic polymer droplets in planar microfluidic T-junction channels using high-speed optical imaging and particle image velocimetry. By varying the capillary number, flow rate ratio, and fluid elasticity, we map transitions between squeezing, dripping, and jetting regimes and derive a scaling law for droplet volume control in lab-on-a-chip synthesis.

membranes.title: Polyelectrolyte multilayer nanofiltration membranes for selective micropollutant removal in wastewater reuse
membranes.abstract: Hollow-fiber nanofiltration membranes fabricated via layer-by-layer assembly of polyelectrolytes are evaluated for high-recovery municipal wastewater reclamation. We measure permeance, monovalent versus divalent ion selectivity, and retention of pharmaceutical micropollutants under cross-flow fouling conditions, demonstrating chemical cleaning stability over extended filtration cycles.

responsibleAi.title: Auditing algorithmic fairness and transparency in public-sector automated decision systems
responsibleAi.abstract: Public administrations increasingly deploy machine learning models for risk assessment and resource allocation, raising legal and ethical concerns around accountability and disparate impact. We combine socio-technical impact assessments with empirical fairness audits under the EU AI Act to propose a participatory governance framework for trustworthy public-sector AI.

manuscript.privacyBody: Embedded locally on this server — your manuscript text is never sent to external AI services or stored.

funder.heading: Do you have a research funder with open-access rules?
funder.description: Selecting a funder checks every candidate journal against its Jisc Open Policy Finder policy and syncs with your browser preference.
funder.yesDesc: Check journals against NWO, Horizon Europe, ERC, ZonMw, or any Jisc Open Policy Finder funder.
funder.noDesc: Prioritize Diamond OA and {institution} agreements without a separate funder check.
funder.selectPrompt: Pick a funder above or search below to check compliance (you can also continue without selecting one).

budget.heading: What is your publishing (APC) budget?
budget.description: Diamond Open Access and active {institution} publishing deals are always prioritized first.
budget.noneDesc: Only €0 publishing options: Diamond OA journals and active {institution} publishing deals.
budget.cappedDesc: Include Gold OA journals up to a maximum fee alongside €0 Diamond OA and institutional deals.
budget.funderPaysDesc: Show all open-access options eligible for grant reimbursement (Diamond and deals still ranked first).
budget.anyDesc: Include every topically relevant venue, including subscription journals, while highlighting OA routes.
budget.capCustomHint: Or enter a custom amount in euros (0 – 50,000)

preferences.heading: Fine-tune your ranking preferences
preferences.description: Every preference is transparent and optional — topical relevance always stays the main signal.
preferences.historyTitle: Boost journals where {institution} researchers already publish
preferences.historyDesc: Adds a gentle familiarity nudge for venues with recent {institution} publications.
preferences.establishedDesc: Adds a modest nudge for ScimagoJR Q1–Q2 journals. Per DORA principles, treat venue indicators as context rather than article quality.
preferences.nonJournalsDesc: Broaden results beyond peer-reviewed journals to include book series and proceedings (e.g. LNCS).

results.heading: Recommended journals
results.subheading: Ranked from {pool} semantically similar venues ({strict} strict {strict, plural, one {match} other {matches}}).
results.moreMatchesIntro: Additional venues matching all of your criteria.
results.alternativesIntro: Fewer than three journals matched every strict rule. These topically close venues show what would change if you relax one constraint (for example via Green OA / Taverne or a higher APC).
results.noResultsBody: Try adding a few more domain keywords or sentences to your abstract, or relax your budget and venue filters.
results.transparencyLead: No black-box AI ranking: your manuscript is embedded locally with bge-small-en-v1.5, matched against journal profiles in PostgreSQL (pgvector), and scored with the deterministic rules below.
